interpretation: Hypothetical one-period stress revaluations of the current fixed-quantity holdings. Not forecasts, predictions or investment advice. Every shock value below is a configurable illustrative assumption unless a scenario states it is replayed from observed dataset closes.

historical_events.name: COVID-19 market crash (2020)
historical_events.window_basis: Analyst-defined approximate NIFTY 50 closing peak and trough dates; verify against NSE Indices before relying on them. No price data for this window is bundled with the project.

historical_events.name: 2022 global inflation and interest-rate shock
historical_events.window_basis: Analyst-defined approximate NIFTY 50 closing peak and trough dates; verify against NSE Indices before relying on them. No price data for this window is bundled with the project.

historical_events.name: Indian general-election result day (4 June 2024)
historical_events.window_basis: Close of the prior session to the close of result day.

historical_events.name: Global risk-off / carry-trade unwind (5 August 2024)
historical_events.window_basis: Close of the prior session to the close of 5 August 2024.

historical_events.name: US tariff shock (7 April 2025)
historical_events.window_basis: Close of the prior session to the close of 7 April 2025.

hypothetical_scenarios.name: Yield +100 bp and USD/INR +5% (rate and FX sensitivities)

assumed_macro_sensitivities.description: Sector-level directional assumptions used only when no source-labelled rate/FX series is supplied. rate_change_pp: return per +1 percentage point (100 bp) change in the 10Y G-sec yield. usdinr_change: return per unit (decimal) USD/INR change, e.g. 0.20 means +1% USD/INR gives +0.2%. These numbers are not estimated from data and must be replaced or confirmed by the user.
